Ajay Mohan Goel, Judge (Oral)

By way of this petition, filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioners have prayed for quashing of FIR No.314 of 2018, dated 18.12.2018, registered under Sections 498A,
406, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, at Nalagarh, District Solan, H.P., inter alia,
on the ground that the issue which led to the registration of the FIR Whether reporters of the local papers may be allowed to see the judgment?

stands amicably settled between the petitioners, i.e. the accused and the complainant, i.e.
respondent No.2 as the marriage .
between petitioner No.1 and respondent No.2 stands dissolved by way of a mutual divorce.
2. Notices were issued to respondent No.2 on 02.03.2023.
Today, said respondent is present in the Court in person.
As she has not engaged any Lawyer, therefore, the Court has requested Ms. Tanu Sharma, learned counsel, who is present in the Court, to assist the Court as learned Legal Aid Counsel.
Learned Counsel was requested by the Court to talk with respondent No.2 for some time and apprise her consequences of the prayer made in the petition.

The hearing of the case was deferred for some time and thereafter, learned Counsel informed the Court that she discussed the matter with respondent No.2 and apprised her that the petition was filed for quashing of the FIR lodged by her on the ground that the matter between her and the petitioners, i.e. the accused stands settled and the parties have now agreed to put an end to their issues and disputes as stand spelled out in the petition.

Learned Counsel further informed the Court that respondent No.2 has told her that she is aware of the contents of the petition and she agrees to the averments made therein and she has no objection in case the present petition is allowed, as prayed for, and the FIR as also the ensuing criminal proceedings are quashed and set aside as a .
mutual divorce stands granted to petitioner No.1 and her by the competent Court of Law.

Thereafter,
her statement to this effect was recorded in the Court, in which again she reiterated that as the marriage between her and petitioner No.1 has been dissolved by way of a mutual divorce and she has thereafter remarried, therefore, she has no objection in case the present petition is allowed and FIR as also the ensuing criminal proceedings are quashed and set aside.

3. Accordingly, in view of the above narrated facts as the issue which led to the registration of the FIR now stands resolved between the parties and statement of respondent No.2 recorded to this effect, this petition is allowed by quashing FIR No.314 of 2018, dated 18.12.2018, registered under Sections 498A, 406, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, at Nalagarh, District Solan,
Akhilesh Kumar & Others vs The State Of Himachal Pradesh & Another on 19 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/82270706/
2 H.P., so also the ensuing criminal proceedings, i.e. Case No.156/2 of 2019, pending in the Court of learned Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Nalagarh, District Solan, H.P.
4.
